title: Cycle structure of the Pollard-rho map x^2+c mod n: three new exact sequences (and a calibration against A352635)
description: Exact functional-graph statistics of the quadratic map f(x) = x^2 + c (mod n), the iteration at the heart of Pollard's (1975) rho factoring method. Iterating f turns Z_n into a functional graph (out-degree 1 everywhere), so each component is one cycle with trees draining in. PRIMARY RESULT: three sequences computed exactly, (1) the number of PERIODIC POINTS of x^2+1 mod n, n=1..1000 (1,2,1,2,3,2,2,2,3,6,2,2,6,4,3,2,6,6,2,6,...), the natural sibling of the catalogued CYCLE count A352635 (Chai Wah Wu), which counts cycles of the same map but not its periodic points; (2) Sum over c=0..n-1 of the number of periodic points of x^2+c mod n, n=1..400 (1,4,5,8,12,20,16,16,27,48,...); (3) Sum over c=0..n-1 of the number of cycles of x^2+c mod n, n=1..400 (1,3,4,6,8,13,11,12,17,26,...). TERM COVERAGE, STATED PRECISELY: all 1,800 staged terms (1000 + 400 + 400, index ranges n=1..1000 and n=1..400) are read back off the deposited b-files and recomputed by `node oversight/oeis/pollard-rho-x2plus1/verify-staged.mjs`, which exits nonzero on any mismatch. No staged term is left unrecomputed and none rests on a stored expected-value table. Each term is recomputed TWO WAYS, and what differs between the two is: (A) analyze() in research/pollard-rho/engine.mjs, a depth-first path walk with three-colour marking that discovers a cycle when a walk re-enters itself, using the shared mapFn closure, which is also the engine that generated the files, so on its own it is drift protection rather than independence; and (B) peelPeriodic() in verify-staged.mjs, which shares no code with (A), recomputes f inline instead of calling mapFn, and finds the cyclic set by in-degree peeling (repeatedly delete every node nothing points at; the survivors are exactly the cycles). Both run in one process and one language, so together they exclude an implementation error in either walk and any corruption or staleness in the deposited bytes, but not a shared misreading of the definition. CALIBRATION AGAINST AN EXTERNAL ANSWER: both (A) and (B) reproduce A352635 (cycles of x^2+1 mod n) for ALL n=1..1000, checked against terms downloaded from the OEIS b-file https://oeis.org/A352635/b352635.txt and committed as a352635-reference.mjs. This covers the full staged index range but certifies the machinery, not the staged values, since A352635 counts a different statistic of the same graph. Separately, research/pollard-rho/verify.mjs cross-checks analyze() against a from-scratch brute force for all n<=200 and c in {0,1,2,3,5} on cycles, periodic points, fixed points and longest cycle; that check does not read the b-files and reaches only one fifth of the staged range of the periodic sequence. ABSENCE FROM THE OEIS: checked 2026-07-27, one search window per sequence (20 terms for the periodic sequence, 16 for each Sum_c sequence), all three returning no catalogued match; the exact URLs and exact answers are in absence-2026-07-27.json, together with a positive control (factorials, which correctly returned A000142) and a negative control (a contrived sequence, which correctly returned nothing). CONTEXT ESTABLISHED IN THE SAME WORK (verified, not staged as sequences): Pollard's rho factors a battery of five semiprimes plus one mixed composite, the largest a balanced 10-digit semiprime 3037000493 x 3037000507 (about 9.2e18) in roughly 7e4 iterations; the iteration reduced mod a prime factor p collides in O(sqrt p) steps (the hidden 'small rho' the gcd detects), >=100x sooner than the sqrt(pi*N/2) scale of a rho mod N; averaged over all generic c the mean rho length of x^2+c mod p matches Flajolet-Odlyzko's random-map prediction sqrt(pi*p/2) (committed assertion: a 6% bound; worst deviation actually measured over p in {401,809,1601,3209,6421}: 3.2%; this one is empirical, since x^2+c is conjectured random-like, not proved so); and the two textbook 'avoid' values are exactly the non-random ones, c=0 (x->x^2) having periodic-point count EXACTLY 1 + oddpart(p-1), derived in research/pollard-rho/special-c.md and checked against all primes p<2000, and c=-2 (the Chebyshev / Lucas-Lehmer map) deviating from the random prediction far more than generic c. Reproduce from bundled code: `node oversight/oeis/pollard-rho-x2plus1/verify-staged.mjs` (the artifact gate over all 1,800 deposited terms, 2.4 s measured 2026-07-27) and `node research/pollard-rho/verify.mjs` (26/26, the engine and every claim above, 8.6 s measured 2026-07-27). A third script, derive.mjs, regenerates the b-files; it is a producer and is not part of verification. PROVENANCE: the computation and prose were produced by an AI instance (Claude) within the open 'Artificial Wasteland' project, under a strict never-lie / show-the-check rule; deposited as a citable, independently-checkable artifact and explicitly offered for independent human verification. Per OEIS policy it has NOT been submitted to OEIS by the project; any OEIS entry or comment should be authored only by a human who has verified it themselves.

Calibration sequence (catalogued, reproduced exactly for all n=1..1000 against the OEIS b-file): A352635 = cycles of x^2+1 mod n = 1,1,1,1,1,1,2,1,1,1,1,1,3,2,1,1,1,1,2,1. Corrections made 2026-07-27, recorded here because the earlier deposit text was wrong: the score of research/pollard-rho/verify.mjs was stated as 17/17 and is 26/26; the phrase 'cross-checked two independent ways' was a blanket claim although the two-way check reached only n<=200 and no script read the b-files at all; the absence check was dated 2026-06-25 with no committed log and has been withdrawn and re-run; and the factoring battery's largest entry was described as a balanced 10-digit semiprime 3037000499 x 3037000493, but 3037000499 is not prime (13 x 233615423), so it was not a semiprime and rho found the factor 13 in 4 iterations, demonstrating nothing about the balanced case. The battery now uses 3037000493 x 3037000507.
